title: Driller
build: Incentive Software's original 48K tape (TOSEC: Driller (1987)(Incentive).tzx), a BASIC loader, a 448-byte loader code block and three turbo blocks: the loading screen, 37,590 bytes of game at $6B12-$FDE7 and the game's own screen

tools.emulator: release ZEsarUX-13.0, ZEsarUX_linux-13.0-ubuntu24_x86_64.tar.gz, run as a Spectrum 48K; check-emulator 47 of 50 on 2 November 2026 (count-while-running, load-keeps-frame-phase and warp, each with a workaround in kit/skills/spectrum/tool-zesarux)
tools.checker: a second session of the same model, briefed cold, for the listing sample
tools.host: Linux x86_64 (Ubuntu 24.04, no display), a hosted cloud session

accuracy.note: the port was written first, routine by routine in lockstep with the game, and the listing's comments on code were written from it, so it found none of them wrong
75 of the 262 comments; each of the 14 was wrong in a detail, and all 14 were corrected

exclude: the printer buffer and the ROM's system variables: the game reads FRAMES ($5C78) once, to start its frame counter, and keeps the ROM's IY for the tape routines, and has no data of its own here

the game's work buffers, written in play (the view buffer and the multiply routines at $5CBC, the matrix and vertices at $5E4C, the object buffer at $5F4D, the draw list at $6766, the face list at $6856); at the hand-over they still hold the BASIC loader

not the game's block: the loader the BASIC puts at $FE40, which loads the game and hands over, and the bytes below it; the game fills $FE00-$FF00 with its interrupt table, puts a jump at $FDFD and keeps its stack below $FFF8
include: the game's own screen, loaded from the tape as its last block: the cockpit and the console, which the game draws its view and its figures into
